title: Gatekeeper digital platforms
summary: A few global platforms control app distribution on mobile phones, general search and much of digital advertising. Over its five-year Digital Platform Services Inquiry (2020 to 2025) the ACCC found competition problems in these markets and recommended new rules for designated platforms.
direction_rationale: Platforms that are also gatekeepers can set terms for, and favour their own services over, the businesses that depend on them.

industries.name: Internet Service Providers and Web Search Portals

verified.notes: A market structure, not a law: no dates. ACCC pages refuse automated requests; the findings are from search excerpts of the ACCC's report and press coverage, not read in full.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 28 October 2026 (phase 4 of the productivity framework pivot) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: A handful of platforms control app stores, search and digital advertising. Businesses that depend on them face the platforms' terms and self-preferencing, which can blunt competition and new services.

marks.reason: Gatekeeper platforms face little competition in app distribution, search and ad tech.
Platform rules and self-preferencing can disadvantage rival apps and services.
